'''OnlyFans''' is an Internet content paid [[subscription service]] based in [[London]], England.<ref name="RS May20">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-features/onlyfans-sex-workers-porn-creators-999881/ |title=Sex Workers Built OnlyFans. Now They Say They're Getting Kicked Off |first1=E. J. |last1=Dickson |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=18 May 2020 |access-date=15 May 2021 |archive-date=23 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423103841/https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-features/onlyfans-sex-workers-porn-creators-999881/ |url-status=live |url-access=limited}}</ref> The service is widely known for its popularity with [[pornography|pornographers]],<ref name="RS May20"/><ref name="BBC News 2021"/> but it also hosts other content creators, including athletes, musicians, and comedians.<ref name="Esq1" /><ref>{{Cite news |agency=Associated Press |date=7 December 2023 |title=Australian tennis star Nick Kyrgios joins OnlyFans to create new athlete content |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2023/dec/08/nick-kyrgios-onlyfans-account-australian-tennis-star |access-date=15 April 2025 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=23 October 2023 |title=Whitney Cummings to Release Her First Stand-Up Comedy Special for OnlyFans' SFW Free Streaming Service |url=https://variety.com/2023/digital/news/whitney-cummings-onlyfans-first-stand-up-comedy-special-free-oftv-1235765150/ |access-date=15 April 2025 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

Content on the platform is user-generated and monetized via monthly subscriptions, tips, and [[pay-per-view]]. Creators are paid 80% of these fees and earn a yearly average of $1,300. In 2021, the company launched a free [[safe-for-work]] streaming platform, OFTV. OnlyFans grew in popularity during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. {{As of|2024}}, the site had more than four million registered creators and 370 million registered users.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Berg |first1=Madeline |title=6 OnlyFans stats that show how massive the platform has become |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/onlyfans-app-surges-creators-users-revenue-owner-leonid-radvinsky-earnings-2025-8 |access-date=12 October 2025 |publisher=Business Insider |date=22 August 2025}}</ref>

In August 2021, a campaign to investigate the company began in the [[United States Congress]], and it was reported that from October 2021 onward it would no longer allow sexually explicit material,<ref name="BBC News 2021">{{cite news |title=OnlyFans to ban sexually explicit content |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-58273914 |access-date=20 August 2021 |work=BBC News |date=20 August 2021 |archive-date=20 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210820004312/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-58273914 |url-status=live}}</ref> due to pressure from banks that OnlyFans used for user payments. ==Overview==
OnlyFans is a British [[subscription business model|subscription-based]] [[video on demand]] service and social media network.<ref name="RS May20" /> It acts as a [[video hosting service]], allowing [[content creation|content creators]] to upload videos and garner subscribers to their content.<ref name="Insider1"/> As such, it is part of the [[creator economy]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://time.com/6124508/creator-economy-onlyfans-twitch-future/ |title=How 'Subscribe to Me' Became the Future of Work |magazine=Time |location=New York |last=Bruner |first=Raisa |date=1 December 2021 |access-date=24 October 2023 |url-access=limited}}</ref> Subscribers pay creators in monthly instalments, in one-time tips, or via [[pay-per-view]]. The company takes 20% of these fees.<ref name="Insider1">{{cite news |title=We spoke to a woman earning more than $100,000 a year selling explicit content on OnlyFans — this is exactly how she makes her money |last1=Jankowicz |first1=Mia |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/onlyfans-monica-huldt-describes-how-makes-money-2020-3 |work=Business Insider |date=14 March 2020 |access-date=22 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="NYT1">{{cite news |title=How OnlyFans Changed Sex Work Forever |last1=Bernstein |first1=Jacob |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/02/09/style/onlyfans-porn-stars.html |work=The New York Times |date=9 February 2019 |access-date=22 May 2023 |url-access=limited}}</ref>

OnlyFans is an Internet content paid subscription service based in London, England. The service is widely known for its popularity with pornographers, but it also hosts other content creators, including athletes, musicians, and comedians.
Content on the platform is user-generated and monetized via monthly subscriptions, tips, and pay-per-view. Creators are paid 80% of these fees and earn a yearly average of $1,300. In August 2021, a campaign to investigate the company began in the United States Congress, and it was reported that from October 2021 onward it would no longer allow sexually explicit material, due to pressure from banks that OnlyFans used for user payments. This decision was reversed six days later due to backlash from users and creators.
